BXL-00014-A-29.headline: Calls for official data and action on gynaecological violence
BXL-00014-A-29.source_brief: This resolution, defended by DéFI's Gisèle Mandaila and Ecolo's Margaux De Ré, asks the Region to recognise and act against gynaecological and obstetric violence, noting Belgium lacks official statistics or a structured reporting system for it. It calls for better data collection, awareness and more respectful, consent-based medical care during pregnancy and childbirth. Parliament adopted it with 62 votes for and 20 abstentions, the abstentions coming from the MR group.
BXL-00014-A-29.stake: It shapes how patients are informed and treated during pregnancy, childbirth and perinatal care.

BXL-00014-A-192.headline: Asks all 19 communes to create safe spaces for women
BXL-00014-A-192.source_brief: Presented by Ecolo's Farida Tahar and inspired by a motion passed unanimously in Schaerbeek, this resolution seeks to combat sexist and sexual violence against women, including in political and institutional settings. It sets out six lines of action, encouraging all 19 communes to adopt charters, training, clear independent reporting procedures, prevention and gender mainstreaming. Parliament adopted it unanimously, all groups voting in favour.
BXL-00014-A-192.stake: It aims to make workplaces, institutions and public life safer for women across Brussels.

BXL-00014-A-145.headline: Reform of jobseeker availability checks rejected almost unanimously
BXL-00014-A-145.source_brief: Originally tabled by DéFI and Anders, this resolution sought to abolish the three-member evaluation panel used by Actiris when checking jobseekers' availability for work, while leaving the minister flexibility to set control deadlines. In committee the text was reshaped by MR and cd&v amendments imposing a more rigid framework. The final amended version was rejected by Parliament, with 1 vote for, 80 against and 1 abstention.
BXL-00014-A-145.stake: It affects how unemployed Brussels residents' job-search efforts are checked and which can affect their benefits.

BXL-00014-A-236.headline: Backs the Iranian people and condemns the regime's crackdown
BXL-00014-A-236.source_brief: Tabled by the PS's Latifa Aït Baala with Marc-Jean Ghyssels and Jamal Ikazban, and co-signed across several groups, this resolution responds to the violent repression of peaceful protests in Iran since late December 2025. It calls for Parliament to support the Iranian population, defend their fundamental rights and condemn the regime's crackdown. Parliament adopted it with most members in favour, while the PTB and Open VLD abstained.
BXL-00014-A-236.stake: It states the Region's official position on human rights abroad, using its international standing as a host of EU and NATO institutions.
